# Posewise

> Posewise is an iPhone app that uses the phone's camera to check yoga pose alignment. It measures joint angles from the side or front, speaks corrections out loud while you hold the pose, and builds a short daily workout (about six minutes) of the strength, flexibility and mobility exercises that address the specific faults it found. Pose detection runs on the device; no video is uploaded. It covers 14 poses and is currently in beta.

## Pose guides

- [How to improve your Downward Dog](https://posewise.app/poses/downward-dog): the five things that usually hold back Downward Dog (tight hamstrings, tight calves, stiff shoulders, weak pressing strength, stiff wrists), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Warrior II](https://posewise.app/poses/warrior-2): the five things that usually hold back Warrior II (leg strength for a 90° front knee, outer-hip strength for knee tracking, tight groin and quads bending the back leg, core strength for an upright torso, shoulder endurance for level arms), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Warrior I](https://posewise.app/poses/warrior-1): the five things that usually hold back Warrior I (leg strength for a 90° front knee, tight calves lifting the back heel and bending the back leg, tight hip flexors tipping the torso and twisting the hips, outer-hip strength for knee tracking, shoulder mobility for arms overhead), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Upward Dog](https://posewise.app/poses/upward-dog): the four things that usually hold back Upward Dog (pressing strength for straight arms, upper-back mobility so the bend doesn’t pinch the low back, glute and leg strength to lift the thighs, shoulder mobility to stack the shoulders over the wrists), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Chair Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/chair): the four things that usually hold back Chair Pose (leg strength to sit low without the knees driving forward, ankle mobility to let the shins tip forward, core control for a steady forward lean, shoulder mobility for arms overhead), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Crescent Lunge](https://posewise.app/poses/crescent-lunge): the three things that usually hold back Crescent Lunge (leg strength for a 90° front knee, tight hip flexors and quads bending the back leg and tipping the torso, shoulder mobility for arms overhead), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Extended Side Angle](https://posewise.app/poses/extended-side-angle): the four things that usually hold back Extended Side Angle (leg strength for a 90° front knee, tight groin and quads bending the back leg, tight calves lifting the back heel, stiff shoulders breaking the top-arm line), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Goddess Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/goddess): the four things that usually hold back Goddess Pose (leg strength for squat depth, outer-hip strength for knee tracking, core strength for an upright torso, shoulder mobility for even cactus arms), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Triangle Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/triangle): the three things that usually hold back Triangle Pose (tight hamstrings bending the front knee or collapsing the torso, stiff shoulders pulling the top arm off vertical, a stiff upper back keeping the chest facing down), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Tree Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/tree): the three things that usually hold back Tree Pose (outer-hip strength for level hips and an upright torso, quad strength for a straight standing leg, core strength for a steady head and balance), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Cobra Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/cobra): the two things that usually hold back Cobra Pose (a stiff upper back that sends the bend into the low back and neck, and pelvic control to keep the hips grounded), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Bridge Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/bridge): the three things that usually hold back Bridge Pose (glute and hamstring strength for hip height, core control so the low back doesn’t do the lifting, a neutral neck under load), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Mountain Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/mountain): the two things that usually hold back Mountain Pose (core control for an upright, stacked torso, and a stiff upper back and neck pushing the head forward), with the alignment rubric and a daily exercise for each.
- [How to improve your Child’s Pose](https://posewise.app/poses/childs-pose): the two things that usually keep Child’s Pose from feeling restful (tight lats and shoulders making the forward reach work, and a neck that won’t let go), with the alignment rubric and a gentle daily exercise for each.

## About

- [Home](https://posewise.app/): what Posewise does, the poses it covers, and how to join the beta.
